source: REAL data — default=1: the client defaulted on the payment due in October 2005 ("default payment next month"). Source: Yeh, I-Cheng. Default of Credit Card Clients [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository, 2009. https://doi.org/10.24432/C55S3H — introduced in Yeh & Lien, "The comparisons of data mining techniques for the predictive accuracy of probability of default of credit card clients", Expert Systems with Applications 36 (2009), DOI 10.1016/j.eswa.2007.12.020. What it is: real credit-card clients of a bank in Taiwan, April–September 2005. Licence: CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) — redistribution of this subset is permitted with attribution. Rows: 30,000 published, 35 exact duplicates removed, 29,965 usable (6,630 positive, base rate 22.13%). Features: creditLimit (NT$), payStatusSep…payStatusApr (repayment status Sept→April 2005 as published: −2/−1/0 on-time states, 1–8 months late), billSep/billAug/billJul (bill amounts), paidSep/paidAug/paidJul (amounts paid), utilisationSep = billSep / creditLimit (derived). Sex, education, marital status and age are deliberately left out (protected characteristics); the three oldest bills and payments are left out to stay within 16 features. Split: interleaved by client order after de-duplication — 3 clients in every 10 (i mod 10 < 3) are held out; the brain grew only on the other 7; natural class mix (no thinning); training pool thinned evenly to 20,000 rows (class-stratified). The brain grew on 20,000 training rows only. This file: 1,500 of the 8,991 held-out rows, evenly spaced and class-stratified — 1,500 rows, 343 positive (22.87%); none were seen in growth.
